# Aurora Night Navigation Launch

Meet Aurora, our night-time navigation product for safer routes after dark. Its low-light guidance highlights well-lit streets, late transit connections, and accessible paths.

Aurora launches on 12 January with privacy-first location controls and downloadable city maps.

# Aurora: Find a Brighter Way Home

After sunset, finding a comfortable route should not be guesswork. Aurora guides people through illuminated streets, dependable evening transport, and step-free paths while keeping location history private.

The night navigation service arrives 12 January, with offline city maps included.

# See Aurora Live

Join our evening product demonstration at North Dock Hall. The team will show route planning, offline maps, and low-light guidance before a public question session.

# Why Heritage Apples Matter

Small orchards preserve fruit varieties such as Ashmead's Kernel and Egremont Russet. Their sharp flavours, resilient trees, and varied harvest windows help growers build healthier local food systems.

# Apple Services Lift Quarterly Revenue

Apple reported stronger services revenue alongside steady iPhone demand. Investors focused on margins, installed-device growth, and the company's capital-return programme rather than fruit or agricultural markets.

# QuasarEdge QX-417 Release Notes

The QX-417 controller adds deterministic failover for orbital telemetry gateways. QuasarEdge operators can now rotate signing keys without interrupting packet ingestion.

# SASE Without the Jargon

Secure Access Service Edge, or SASE, combines network access and cloud-delivered security policy. It gives distributed teams consistent protection without routing every connection through a headquarters appliance.

# Trust No Connection by Default

Modern security checks identity, device health, and context for each request. This verification model limits lateral movement and replaces broad network trust with narrowly granted access.

# Kyoto Before the Crowds

Walk the Philosopher's Path shortly after sunrise, pause at a neighbourhood kissaten, and visit smaller temple gardens in northern Higashiyama. Slow mornings reveal the city's calm details.

# A Long Weekend in Lisbon

Ride the ferry for skyline views, explore tiled streets in Alfama, and finish with contemporary Portuguese cooking in Arroios. Leave room for an unplanned miradouro at sunset.

# Meridian Labs Acquires Northstar Analytics

Meridian Labs today announced its acquisition of Northstar Analytics, expanding its supply-chain forecasting capabilities. The transaction is expected to close in the second quarter, subject to customary conditions.

# Meridian Labs to Acquire Northstar Analytics

Meridian Labs has agreed to acquire Northstar Analytics to strengthen predictive planning for global supply chains. Closing is anticipated in Q2 following customary regulatory and contractual conditions.

# Northstar Customer Forum 2026

Operations leaders will meet in Rotterdam for forecasting workshops, customer panels, and hands-on planning clinics. Registration includes the evening harbour reception.

# Building Patiently in Public

This quarter reminded me that durable companies are built through small promises kept consistently. I am grateful to our customers for candid feedback and to the team for turning it into better work.

# Carbon Border Rules Enter the Reporting Phase

Importers must prepare embedded-emissions records before certificate purchasing begins. The policy aims to align the carbon cost of domestic production and selected imports while preserving documented exemptions.

# Advanced Packaging Becomes the Capacity Constraint

Demand for AI accelerators is shifting attention from wafer supply to high-bandwidth memory and advanced packaging. Lead times remain uneven even as conventional chip inventories normalize.

# Helios Brings Shared Solar to Apartment Buildings

Helios lets residents subscribe to nearby rooftop generation without installing panels on their own homes. Monthly statements show allocated production, bill credits, and avoided emissions.

# Lumen Makes Offices Responsive

Lumen adjusts workplace lighting to occupancy and daylight, reducing wasted electricity while maintaining comfortable desks and meeting rooms. Facilities teams manage zones from one dashboard.

# Riverstone Responsible AI Summit

Researchers, policy leaders, and product teams will gather on 18 March to discuss practical model governance. Sessions cover audit evidence, incident response, and accountable deployment.

# What We Learned at Riverstone

The responsible AI summit moved beyond principles toward operational evidence. Speakers emphasized incident drills, traceable decisions, and governance that product teams can actually follow.

# FinOps Turns Cloud Cost Into a Team Habit

Engineering, finance, and product leaders share timely usage data and ownership. The practice connects architecture decisions with unit economics instead of treating the cloud bill as a monthly surprise.

# Private Spaces Arrive in Atlas

Atlas users can now create encrypted project spaces with expiring guest access. Administrators receive access-event records without visibility into protected document contents.

# Atlas Adds Offline Trail Maps

Hikers can download topographic regions, mark water sources, and navigate without mobile coverage. Battery-aware location sampling keeps routes available on longer trips.

user_request: Produce the annual resilient logistics report
content:
# Resilient Logistics Outlook 2026

## Executive summary
Supply networks are moving from emergency buffers toward selective resilience. Operators are mapping critical dependencies, measuring recovery time, and reserving capacity where substitution is genuinely difficult. The strongest programmes connect commercial priorities with operational signals rather than applying the same inventory policy everywhere.

## Port operations
Ports are adopting appointment systems and shared arrival data to reduce queues. Better coordination between terminals, carriers, and inland transport makes capacity more predictable. Digital documents shorten handoffs, but participants still need common exception procedures when data arrives late or conflicts.

## Rail corridors
Cross-border rail is gaining attention for stable transit times and lower emissions. Growth depends on terminal interoperability, locomotive availability, and reliable customs processes. Shippers increasingly compare total variability rather than headline speed when choosing between rail and road.

## Ocean freight
Contract design now includes clearer allocation rules for disruption periods. Importers are diversifying sailings while avoiding fragmentation across too many carriers. Visibility tools help teams identify rolled containers early, although operational relationships remain essential when schedules deteriorate.

## Air cargo
High-value components and urgent healthcare products continue to support air demand. Procurement teams are negotiating flexible block-space agreements instead of relying entirely on spot markets. Carbon reporting is becoming part of routing decisions alongside cost and service.

## Warehouse automation
Robotics investment is shifting toward modular systems that can be deployed without rebuilding entire sites. Operators prioritize measurable throughput, safe human interaction, and maintainable software. Flexible automation is especially valuable during seasonal peaks and changing product mixes.

## Cold chain
Temperature-sensitive networks need evidence across every custody transfer. Low-power sensors, calibrated packaging, and rapid exception response reduce spoilage risk. Healthcare and food operators are also testing shared standards so partners can exchange records without manual reconciliation.

## Supplier risk
Leading companies combine financial indicators with operational observations such as lead-time drift and quality incidents. Supplier conversations remain important because dashboards rarely capture emerging constraints soon enough. Dual sourcing helps only when alternatives have qualified capacity and distinct dependencies.

## Inventory strategy
Blanket stock increases are giving way to segmented policies. Teams consider demand volatility, substitution options, replenishment time, and margin exposure for each category. Scenario exercises reveal where modest buffers protect revenue and where extra inventory merely hides planning problems.

## Data standards
Shared identifiers and event definitions are prerequisites for useful network visibility. Companies are investing in governance for milestone data, ownership, and correction workflows. A smaller trusted dataset often creates more value than a broad feed nobody can explain.

## Climate adaptation
Flood, heat, and wildfire risks are entering facility and route planning. Businesses are evaluating alternate gateways and backup power while working with local authorities on infrastructure resilience. Adaptation plans need trigger points, responsible owners, and funded actions rather than generic risk statements.

## Procurement and workforce
Procurement teams now evaluate continuity evidence, transparent capacity assumptions, exception communication, and tested recovery plans alongside price. Multi-year agreements include review points for changing operating assumptions. Companies also cross-train planners, warehouse supervisors, customs specialists, and customer teams. Realistic exercises use incomplete information so decision makers practice authority, escalation, and trade-offs before disruption occurs.

## Cyber resilience
Connected logistics platforms create efficiency and a wider attack surface. Operators separate critical systems, verify backups, test manual fallbacks, and rehearse recovery with technology partners. Technical controls are not sufficient by themselves. Teams also maintain current contacts, explicit decision rights, and an agreed sequence for restoring the services customers depend on most.

## Customer communication
During disruption, customers value credible choices more than optimistic estimates. Leading teams explain what is known, what remains uncertain, and when the next update will arrive. They offer alternatives based on business impact instead of sending identical delay notices. Shared internal facts keep sales, service, and operations from giving conflicting accounts of the same event.

## Insurance and finance
Risk financing is becoming more closely connected to operational controls. Insurers request evidence of supplier mapping, facility protection, and tested continuity plans. Finance teams model liquidity effects alongside physical delays because longer transit times can increase working capital sharply. Better operational evidence supports underwriting conversations and helps leaders compare mitigation investments on consistent assumptions.

## Regionalization
Some businesses are adding regional suppliers and assembly options, but regionalization is not automatic simplification. Local networks can still depend on imported materials, specialist tools, concentrated energy infrastructure, or a single transport corridor. Decision makers therefore trace several tiers of dependency and compare recovery characteristics rather than relying only on geographic distance from customers.

## Measurement and governance
Traditional service and cost measures do not fully describe resilience. Teams add time to detect, time to decide, time to recover, and customer impact avoided. These measures work best when attached to specific scenarios. Executive governance assigns owners to critical dependencies, reviews whether mitigations actually exist, and distinguishes consciously accepted exposure from forgotten work.

## Planning cadence
Quarterly network reviews are replacing static annual continuity documents. Planners revisit demand shifts, carrier performance, supplier changes, facility constraints, and political developments using common scenarios. Decisions are recorded with triggers for reconsideration. This cadence helps teams act on gradual deterioration before it becomes an emergency and prevents old assumptions from surviving merely because they were once approved.

## Technology selection
Visibility technology creates value when it supports a defined operational decision. Teams increasingly begin with exception workflows, accountable users, and required response times before selecting data feeds or dashboards. They test coverage and latency against actual shipments. This approach reduces expensive integrations that display movement but do not help anyone choose a better response.

## Scenario rehearsal
Scenario rehearsal turns written plans into observable capability. Teams simulate a blocked gateway, unavailable supplier, technology outage, or sudden demand shift and then record where decisions stalled. Facilitators vary assumptions so participants cannot memorize a response. Follow-up work assigns owners and dates to missing data, unclear authority, fragile communications, and untested alternatives. Repeating the exercise reveals whether improvements survive staff changes and whether recovery estimates match actual operational performance. Customer, finance, legal, technology, and frontline perspectives should participate because a technically feasible response may create unacceptable commercial or regulatory consequences elsewhere in the business.

## Outlook
The next phase of resilience will be disciplined and selective. Organisations that link customer commitments, operational evidence, and rehearsed recovery options will respond faster without carrying unnecessary cost across the whole network.
